title: China Forced Nepal to Cancel an International Conference on Tibetan Studies
gist: The Nepali government forced organizers to cancel the 17th IATS Seminar on Tibetan Studies at Kathmandu University just weeks before it was to open, shifting it online and citing 'security concerns' — a move the author frames as evidence of Beijing's expanding grip over the study and control of Tibetan Buddhism abroad.

themes.theme: Beijing's pressure on Nepal over Tibet

insights.claim: The 17th Seminar of the International Association for Tibetan Studies (IATS), scheduled to be held at Kathmandu University, Nepal from August 23-29, 2026, was cancelled by the organizers on August 5 at the formal request of the Nepali government, and later shifted online.
insights.speaker: Rituja Ghosh
insights.so_what: Signals Kathmandu's willingness to override its own academic institutions on short notice under external pressure, a leading indicator of Nepal's tightening alignment with Beijing on Tibet-sensitive issues.
insights.quote: The 17th Seminar of the International Association for Tibetan Studies (IATS) Conference, scheduled to be held at Kathmandu University, Nepal, from August 23-29, was cancelled on August 5 and later shifted online.
insights.locator: The 17th Seminar of the International Association

insights.claim: The official justification given for cancelling the IATS conference was 'security concerns.'
insights.speaker: Rituja Ghosh
insights.so_what: A vague security rationale for cancelling an academic conference is a marker to watch for similar politically-motivated cancellations of China-sensitive events elsewhere in South Asia.
insights.quote: The abrupt cancellation of the conference on grounds of “security concerns” highlights both Beijing’s ironclad grip and bid to assert authority over Tibetan Buddhism.
insights.locator: The abrupt cancellation of the conference

insights.claim: The author frames the cancellation as evidence of Beijing's ironclad grip over Nepal and its bid to assert authority over Tibetan Buddhism beyond China's own borders.
insights.speaker: Rituja Ghosh
insights.so_what: Suggests China is actively using diplomatic leverage over Nepal to suppress international scholarly engagement with Tibetan religious and cultural topics, a template that could recur with other neighboring states.
insights.quote: highlights both Beijing’s ironclad grip and bid to assert authority over Tibetan Buddhism

insights.claim: The IATS conference is described as one of the premier academic forums for Tibetan culture, history, language and religion, and was set to bring together scholars from 40 countries, including India, China and the United States, many of whom had already arranged and paid for travel to Kathmandu.
insights.speaker: Rituja Ghosh
insights.so_what: The late-notice cancellation imposed direct financial and logistical costs on scholars from major powers including the US, China and India, illustrating how Tibet-related political sensitivities can disrupt cross-border academic exchange.
insights.quote: The conference was set to bring together scholars from 40 countries, including India, China, and the United States – many of whom had already arranged and paid for costs to attend the conference in Kathmandu.
insights.locator: The conference was set to bring together scholars

insights.claim: The conference had been in planning for four years, since Nepal was selected in 2022 to host the seminar.
insights.speaker: Rituja Ghosh
insights.so_what: A four-year planning effort being scrapped weeks before opening underscores how abruptly political pressure can override long-standing institutional commitments in Nepal.
insights.quote: The conference had been in planning for four years, as Nepal was selected to host the seminar in 2022.
insights.locator: The conference had been in planning
